rule.bumpSizing: caret-range semantics: crossing the minor field inside 0.x, or any field inside 0.0.x, counts as major
rule.changesetAwareness: a MEASURED pendingRelease sizes the delta against the projected post-`changeset version` version, credited only when it is strictly ahead of declared AND carries a larger bump; not-measured/absent/indeterminate/absent-from-bump-set fall back to the declared version; adequacy is still the same rank comparison (decision 0024)

THE DS #164 FIX. web dropped ./types/* and shipped as a MINOR (breaks under v1), but a pending changeset projects to 2.0.0 — an adequate MAJOR. Credited, so ok.
MANDATORY ADEQUACY. A removal needs MAJOR; a pending changeset projecting only to 1.1.0 (a MINOR) does not cover it. Still a break — the excuse never excuses an inadequate bump.
FALLBACK. No changeset was measured, so the rule sizes against the declared version — exactly spec-version-1 behaviour. A surface change with no pending bump still breaks.
FALLBACK. The probe ran but this package is not in the computed bump set (newVersion null) — no projection to credit, so the declared bump stands and the removal breaks.

FALLBACK. An indeterminate probe is not a trustworthy projection, so the surface rule grants no credit and the break stands (the ladder separately escalates the probe failure to INDETERMINATE upstream).
An added subpath needs a MINOR; a pending changeset projecting to 1.1.0 covers it. The credit works for additions, not only removals.
PRE.JSON. A prerelease target of the next major (2.0.0-rc.1) is a genuine forward move that crosses the major boundary, so it covers the removal — prerelease-aware, matching bumpBetween.
A prerelease tag on the SAME release triple (1.0.0-rc.1) adds no headroom — not strictly ahead of 1.0.0 — so it is not credited and the removal breaks.

CREDIT ONLY RAISES. A projection BELOW the declared version (1.2.0 < 1.5.0) is regression-shaped; bumpBetween would read it as a MAJOR, but isStrictlyAhead refuses it, so the declared MINOR stands and the removal breaks. The excuse can never launder a backward move.
The declared version already carries an adequate MAJOR, so the pending changeset adds no headroom and is not credited (creditedVersion null). The rule passes on the declared bump alone.

BACKWARD COMPAT. An absent pendingRelease field must read as not-measured: this is the real web regression (declared 1.1.0, a MINOR) with no pending field at all, and it breaks exactly as under spec version 1.
